fact_text: Farid Publishers, a Karachi publisher and bookshop, was founded in 1986 by Syed Farid Hussain, the CEO's father, and is run by his son, the CEO.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: The CEO said the company's outlets stock titles from about 250 other Pakistani publishers alongside its own, in sections on history, philosophy, novels, poetry, Islamic literature and motivation.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: Manuscripts from new writers are read personally by the CEO for controversial or religiously sensitive content before the company quotes a fixed printing budget to the author.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: Established authors are approached by the company or come to it themselves, so the company skips the screening and budgeting steps and goes straight to composing, proofing and printing.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: Notable titles include biographies of Altaf Hussain and Dr Aamir Liaquat Hussain's Seerat Ayesha, Fatima Surayya Bajia's autobiography, and works by Justice Agha Rafiq Ahmed Khan and children's writer Khurram Durrani.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: The children's book Ek Kahawat Ek Kahani has run to more than 10 editions and is the CEO's named best seller.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: Urdu yoga books published by the company are exported to readers in India, Dubai, Melbourne and New Jersey, and the CEO said demand for yoga content abroad is stronger than in Pakistan.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: The company has run a Ramadan book fair in Karachi for about 40 years, every year for the full month, which the CEO called a world record for continuous operation.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: Ramadan fair footfall is strongest after iftar, because shoppers fast during the day and the Urdu Bazaar markets in Karachi's Old City close around 5pm during Ramadan.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: After tarawih, which ends around 11 to 11:30 pm, customers have asked for the Ramadan fair to stay open until sehri, a request the CEO said has come in for about five years.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: The CEO said about 70% of the company's business has shifted online, through Facebook, Instagram and its website.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: Walk-in sales have fallen because the Old City location has traffic and parking problems, so many customers order books online instead of visiting the shop.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: Fewer book fairs in Karachi have removed a discounted sales channel, and the CEO said sales through that channel have dropped compared with earlier years.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: The CEO said print runs of Urdu books fell from about 2,000 to 10,000 copies to about 200 to 500 copies, driven by higher paper and binding costs rather than fewer readers.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: The CEO said readership has not fallen; interest has shifted toward motivational books, translated Russian novels, Urdu and English novels, and away from cooking books.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: The CEO said most Pakistani publishers that closed in the five years to January 2026 had not adapted to social media or to changing reader tastes.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: The CEO's rule of thumb is that a publisher should first understand the reader's mindset and then publish titles that match it, since readers then seek that publisher out.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: The CEO said writers complain of poor royalties from some publishers, which pushes them to self-publish; Farid Publishers says it agrees fixed royalties with its established authors.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)

fact_text: The CEO said writing and printing are easy for anyone, while the hard part is marketing a book and getting readers to buy it.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Love of Literature to a 50-Year Business: Farid Publishers | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-16)
